ideas: Effects on sleep, attention and outdoor play
Safety risks online versus staying in contact
Alternatives like basic phones for young children

phrases.meaning: pressure from friends to fit in
a simple phone for calls and texts

model: In my opinion, children under twelve shouldn't have their own smartphones. First, too much screen time can really damage their concentration and sleep. Kids get hooked on games and short videos very easily, and their attention span becomes shorter. My nephew is nine, and since he got a smartphone last year, his teacher says he can't focus in class for more than ten minutes. Another reason is safety. With a smartphone, children can easily be exposed to harmful content or talk to strangers, and it's hard for parents to keep an eye on everything. There's also peer pressure on social media, which young kids aren't ready to deal with. Of course, parents want to contact their children in case of emergency, and I understand that. But a basic phone that only makes calls and sends texts would solve that problem. I think in the future, more schools are going to ban smartphones for young students anyway, and my sister is going to give her daughter a basic phone next year. So overall, I believe kids should wait until they're at least twelve.
